title: Ministère de l’Éducation sets out baccalauréat reform for the 2028 session
content: The Ministère de l’Éducation nationale presented on Wednesday the framework of a baccalauréat reform that will first apply to the 2028 session, shifting the balance of assessment towards continuous moderation and reducing the number of final written papers from six to four.

Under the plan, continuous assessment will count for 40 per cent of the final mark, with a national moderation protocol administered by the académies to limit disparities between lycées. The four remaining papers will cover the two core subjects, one specialised subject and a general essay.

Minister Rosine Aubert told a *séance* of recteurs and teachers’ representatives that the reform is meant to reduce the “lottery effect” of a single examination week and to give “a serious, verifiable weight” to two years of work. The Conseil supérieur de l’éducation is expected to deliver its formal opinion in December.

The teachers’ unions gave the plan a divided reception. The Syndicat des enseignants des lycées announced a *préavis de grève* for 12 November, arguing that continuous assessment will reward conformity and add several hundred hours of correcting time without additional staff. Two smaller unions said they would support a pilot phase.

In rural lycées, where subject options are already thin, the reform raises a structural problem: continuous assessment assumes a stable timetable that many small schools cannot guarantee. The recteur of the Marbre académie acknowledged that “timetable harmonisation will take at least two years” and that some option closures are unavoidable.

Parents’ federations welcomed the clarity of the timetable while questioning the reliability of local marking. Students’ organisations opposed the change, arguing that a single final examination remains the only mechanism that gives candidates from weak lycées an equal starting point.

Six académies, including Aurelle, will run the new system in pilot form from the 2026 *rentrée*, with an evaluation scheduled for the autumn of 2027. The ministry has committed to presenting the full regulatory texts before the end of the year.
author: Nadia Belrose, correspondante éducation, bureau d’Aurelle — Presses de Vallonne
